name: bot-detector
description: Reddit account signal analysis — three separate scores (automation, agenda, authenticity), shared by the Chrome extension and the optional Node server.
//type: ESM, deliberately — this is the ONE package in BigBrain that is not CommonJS.
The Chrome extension is the primary artifact and must install with
load-unpacked and zero setup, so the scoring core lives inside extension/lib/
and is loaded directly by an MV3 service worker, which only supports ESM
("type": "module" in manifest.json). The optional Node server imports the
very same files via ../extension/lib/..., so there is one implementation of
the scoring with no build step, no bundler and no copy. Node 22 loads ESM
natively, so honouring the extension's constraint costs nothing here.
skill-backend/ and task-runner/ stay CommonJS; do not 'fix' this to match them.
//dependencies: One, and it is optional at runtime. extension/ and the deterministic scoring
core have NO dependencies and must keep none: they use fetch and node:test
only, per the convention of preferring Node's built-ins to npm packages,
and a dependency there would additionally have to survive being loaded
unbundled by a browser extension. @anthropic-ai/sdk is used by server/
agenda.js alone, for the same Messages API call task-runner already depends
on it for -- pure JS, no compiler and no Homebrew formula, so it satisfies
the convention the same way that one does. server/agenda.js imports it
LAZILY, so `npm install` is not needed to run the extension, the scoring
core, or the deterministic half of the server; a backend started without it
still serves verdicts and reports the missing agenda read rather than dying.
//scripts: Both globs are needed: test/ holds the shared core's suite and server/test/
the backend's. A single test/*.test.js glob silently skips the server.
